page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 33 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is rated as strong in stress-ng tests, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression tasks achieve average performance. However, multi-core performance is weak, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores falling into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth ranking in the bottom 10% and large block uncached read/write bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile, the E2as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. It is suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, and text processing applications that benefit from its 16 GB memory footprint but are constrained by the 2 vCPU limit. It is less suitable for highly parallelized tasks, heavy database operations, or high-throughput web serving, where its benchmark results indicate performance bottlenecks.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it includes a 33 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage.
